'''''Ophrys lutea''''', the '''yellow bee-orchid''', is a species of [[orchid]] native to southern Europe, North Africa, and the [[Middle East]], the range extending from Portugal and Morocco to Syria.<ref name="5623459yhjuw">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=141394 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=ophrys+lutea Altervista Flora Italiana, Ofride gialla, Yellow Bee Orchid]</ref>

== Description of the flower ==
Broad asymmetric lateral [[sepal]]s, dorsal sepal lowered.

Extended [[petal]]s, yellow or with a blue-grey or brown spotted [[velvety]] [[macula]]. Pollinated by male ''[[Andrena]]'' bees. This species is notable among ''[[Ophrys]]'' for the fact that the pollinating bees sit on the [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]] facing away from the [[pollinaria]] instead of facing towards them, and thus collect the pollinaria with their [[abdomen]].

== Subspecies ==
Numerous subspecific names have been proposed, but {{As of|2023|alt=as of Sep 2023}} the following are currently accepted:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ophrys lutea Cav. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:647978-1 |access-date=2023-09-27 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

*''Ophrys lutea'' subsp. ''aspea'' <small>(Devillers-Tersch. & Devillers) Faurh.</small> - Northern Tunisia to Northern Libya
*''Ophrys lutea'' subsp. ''galilaea'' <small>(H.Fleischm. & Bornm.) Soó</small> - Mediterranean
*''Ophrys lutea'' subsp. ''laurensis'' <small>(Geniez & Melki) Kreutz</small> - Sicily
*''Ophrys lutea'' subsp. ''lutea'' <small>Cav.</small> - Western and Central Mediterranean to Crete
*''Ophrys lutea'' subsp. ''phryganae '' <small>(Devillers-Tersch. & Devillers) Melki</small> - Central and Eastern Mediterranean

== Flowering period ==
March to May

== Habitat ==
The orchid grows in full sun or shade on limey dry or damp soils, pastures, and thin woodland.
